cities.name: New York

seo.title: Where to meet in New York
seo.description: Sample guide: places in New York that work for groups, from team meetings to coffee catch-ups, plus how to get around by subway.

cities.intro:
*Sample copy for local development. The real intro comes from the control plane.*

New York is easy to reach and hard to agree on. A group spread across Brooklyn, Queens and Manhattan can spend longer choosing a place than getting there. These guides collect places that work for common plans, chosen so most people can arrive on one subway line.

Pick the kind of plan below, or start with a neighborhood.
cities.transit_notes:
*Sample copy.* Most trips here are by **subway**. A place within a short walk of a station served by several lines, like Union Square or Times Square, is usually the most convenient pick for a mixed group.

- Check weekend service changes before you send the plan.
- Allow extra time for crossing between boroughs at rush hour.
- Citi Bike docks are common near parks if anyone prefers to ride.

seo.title: Where to hold a team meeting in New York
seo.description: Sample guide: quiet, bookable places in Manhattan for a team meeting, near subway lines your whole team can reach.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

A team that works from home most of the week still needs a place to sit together now and then. In Manhattan the hard part isn't finding a venue, it's finding one that's quiet enough to talk, takes a booking, and sits near a station everyone can reach without two transfers. The places below cover a free option, a public one and a bookable one.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

## Before you book

1. **List where everyone starts.** Someone coming from Jersey City has a different trip from someone in Astoria.
2. **Compare travel times, not distance.** A spot two stops from a major hub often beats one that looks central on a map.
3. **Book for the hour you'll meet.** A room that's empty at 10 a.m. may be full at lunch.

## On the day

- Send the address, the nearest station and the room name in one message.
- Bring a charger. Outlets go fast in public spaces.
- If the group is bigger than six, a bookable room is worth the cost because public tables rarely fit everyone together.

Want to see each person's trip side by side? [Plan it on Where2Meet](https://www.where2meet.org/) and let the team vote.

places.label: New York Public Library, Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
places.note: Sample note. Reading rooms suit a quiet working session, and Grand Central and Bryant Park stations are a short walk away.

places.label: Bryant Park
places.note: Sample note. Movable tables and chairs work for an informal check-in on a mild day, with many subway lines close by.

places.label: Nomadworks on Broadway
places.note: Sample note. A coworking space with bookable rooms when the meeting needs a screen, a door and a whiteboard.

seo.title: Where to catch up over coffee in New York
seo.description: Sample guide: coffee shops around Union Square for a quick catch-up, close to subway lines from every borough.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

A coffee catch-up should take an hour, not an afternoon of travel. Union Square sits on a handful of subway lines, so friends coming from Brooklyn, Queens and the Upper West Side can all get there on one train. These cafes are a few minutes' walk from the station.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

- **Go early or late.** Midday is the busiest time around the square.
- **Have a backup.** If the first cafe is full, the next one is a block away.
- **Walk afterwards.** The farmers market runs on several days a week and makes a good second stop.

If you're unsure which spot is quickest for everyone, compare everyone's travel time first and pick the place where the longest trip is shortest.

places.label: Joe Coffee on Union Square West
places.note: Sample note. Steps from the station, so it's an easy landmark when people arrive from different lines.

places.label: Blue Dove Coffee
places.note: Sample note. Another option on the west side of the square if the first stop is too busy to find a table.

places.label: Maman on University Place
places.note: Sample note. A slightly quieter spot a few blocks south, good when the catch-up turns into a longer conversation.

towns.name: Williamsburg

seo.title: Where to meet in Williamsburg, Brooklyn
seo.description: Sample guide: places in Williamsburg for a date night or a weekend hangout, a short ride from Manhattan on the L train.

towns.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

Williamsburg is one stop from Manhattan on the L train and a short walk from the East River ferry. It's a convenient pick when half the group lives in Brooklyn and half across the river.
towns.transit_notes: *Sample copy.* The **L train** at Bedford Avenue is the main way in. The **NYC Ferry** stops at North Williamsburg and South Williamsburg. On weekends, check for L train service changes before you send the plan.

seo.title: Where to go on a date night in Williamsburg
seo.description: Sample guide: wine bars in Williamsburg for a date night, near the Bedford Avenue L stop and easy to reach from Manhattan.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

A date shouldn't start with one person on a train for an hour. Williamsburg works when one of you is in Brooklyn and the other in Manhattan, because the L train makes the trip short for both. These wine bars are small, a little dim and good for talking.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

- **Reserve if you can.** Small bars fill up after 8 p.m. on weekends.
- **Plan the ride home.** Late-night L trains run less often, so check the last convenient train for both of you.
- **Keep a second stop in mind.** A walk along the waterfront is an easy way to continue the evening.

places.label: Woodhul Wine Bar
places.note: Sample note. A small, relaxed bar where you can hear each other, a few minutes' walk from the Lorimer Street stop.

places.label: Pinkerton Wine Bar
places.note: Sample note. Candlelit and low-key, a good pick when you want somewhere quieter than the bars on Bedford Avenue.

places.label: With Others
places.note: Sample note. Close to the Bedford Avenue station, which makes the trip home simple for whoever lives in Manhattan.

seo.title: Where to hang out on a weekend in Williamsburg
seo.description: Sample guide: parks and food markets in Williamsburg for a relaxed weekend with friends, close to the L train and the ferry.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

A weekend hangout works best somewhere with space to spread out and food for every taste. Williamsburg has both along the waterfront, and the ferry makes it an easy trip from Manhattan and Queens.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

1. **Pick a meeting point** inside the park, since the entrances are far apart.
2. **Check the market schedule.** Outdoor food markets usually run on weekends from spring to fall.
3. **Bring a blanket** if you plan to stay a while.

places.label: Domino Park
places.note: Sample note. A waterfront park with seating and views of the bridge, next to the South Williamsburg ferry stop.

places.label: Smorgasburg Williamsburg
places.note: Sample note. An outdoor food market with dozens of stalls, so everyone in the group finds something they like.

places.label: McCarren Park
places.note: Sample note. Big lawns and sports fields near the Nassau Avenue G stop, with plenty of room for a larger group.

cities.name: Ann Arbor

seo.title: Where to meet in Ann Arbor
seo.description: Sample guide: places in Ann Arbor for group dinners and coffee catch-ups, with notes on parking, buses and walking downtown.

cities.intro:
*Sample copy for local development. The real intro comes from the control plane.*

Ann Arbor is compact, but a group coming from campus, Ypsilanti and the suburbs still needs a plan. Downtown and Kerrytown are walkable and have the most choice, so most of these picks are there.
cities.transit_notes:
*Sample copy.* Downtown is walkable from central campus. **TheRide** buses connect downtown with Ypsilanti and the north side.

- Public parking structures are spread across downtown.
- Bike lanes on Division Street and William Street make cycling easy in good weather.

seo.title: Where to have a group dinner in Ann Arbor
seo.description: Sample guide: restaurants in downtown Ann Arbor that take large group reservations, near parking and bus stops.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

A group dinner needs a table for everyone, a menu that suits different diets and a place people can reach without circling for parking. These downtown restaurants take reservations for larger groups.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

- **Book ahead on football weekends.** Downtown fills up fast on game days.
- **Ask about set menus** for groups of eight or more.
- **Share a parking plan.** Name the closest structure in the invite so nobody circles the block.

places.label: Sava's on State Street
places.note: Sample note. A large dining room close to campus, with space for bigger groups when you book ahead.

places.label: Union Rec
places.note: Sample note. Games and a long menu on Main Street, a good choice when the dinner turns into a night out.

places.label: La Serre
places.note: Sample note. A quieter spot in a converted house, better suited to a smaller group that wants to talk.

seo.title: Where to catch up over coffee in Ann Arbor
seo.description: Sample guide: coffee shops in downtown Ann Arbor for a catch-up between classes or meetings, a short walk from campus.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

Downtown Ann Arbor has a coffee shop on nearly every block, so the trick is picking one that's convenient for everyone. These are close to Main Street and a short walk from central campus.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

- Weekday mornings are busy with students; mid-afternoon is calmer.
- Most shops have Wi-Fi if the catch-up turns into a working session.

places.label: Jabal Coffee House
places.note: Sample note. Between campus and Main Street, so it works when one person comes from class and one from downtown.

places.label: Moka & Co
places.note: Sample note. On Main Street near several parking structures, handy for anyone driving in from out of town.

places.label: Curious Coffee
places.note: Sample note. On the north end of Main Street, an easy walk from Kerrytown if you want to browse afterwards.

towns.name: Kerrytown

seo.title: Where to meet in Kerrytown, Ann Arbor
seo.description: Sample guide: places in Kerrytown for a weekend hangout, from the farmers market to delis, a short walk from downtown.

towns.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

Kerrytown is Ann Arbor's market district, a few blocks north of downtown. On Saturdays it's the easiest place in town for a group to meet, eat and wander.
towns.transit_notes: *Sample copy.* Kerrytown is a ten-minute walk from Main Street. There's a parking structure on Ann Street, and several bus routes stop on Fifth Avenue.

seo.title: Where to hang out on a weekend in Kerrytown
seo.description: Sample guide: the farmers market, delis and shops in Kerrytown for a relaxed Saturday with friends or family.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

Saturday mornings in Kerrytown mean the farmers market, a line at the deli and shops to browse. It's an easy plan for a group with mixed tastes, and everything is within a block or two.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

- **Arrive early.** The market is busiest late in the morning.
- **Split up, then regroup.** Pick one landmark to meet at after browsing.
- **Bring cash** for some market stalls.

places.label: Ann Arbor Farmers Market
places.note: Sample note. Open-air stalls on Saturdays, and an easy landmark to meet at before the group heads elsewhere.

places.label: Zingerman's Delicatessen
places.note: Sample note. A local institution for sandwiches, with outdoor seating when the weather allows a long lunch.

places.label: Kerrytown Market & Shops
places.note: Sample note. Indoor shops and food counters, a good backup when the weather turns or the market is too crowded.
